articles.headline: Marvin Harrison Jr. will play for Texans on Sunday in London, coach says
articles.description: Texans wideout Marvin Harrison Jr. will play against the Jacksonville Jaguars in London on Sunday, Houston coach DeMeco Ryans said Wednesday.
articles.headlineJa: マービン・ハリソン・ジュニア、日曜にロンドンでテキサンズの一員として出場へ。コーチが発表
articles.descriptionJa: ヒューストンのデメコ・ライアンズコーチは水曜日、テキサンズのワイドレシーバー、マービン・ハリソン・ジュニアが日曜日にロンドンで行われるジャクソンビル・ジャガーズ戦に出場することを明らかにした。
articles.body:
HOUSTON -- Newly acquired Texans wideout Marvin Harrison Jr. will play against the Jacksonville Jaguars in London on Sunday, Houston coach DeMeco Ryans said Wednesday.

It's a quick turnaround for Harrison, as he just arrived in Houston on Monday. The Texans (1-4) sent 2027 second- and seventh-round picks to the Arizona Cardinals to acquire Harrison and a 2027 sixth-round selection after a disappointing start to his career with the Cards.

Harrison has just five catches on 13 targets for 85 yards and a touchdown this season. But he said Wednesday he views the new chapter as a "great" opportunity as he reunites with his college quarterback C.J. Stroud. They played together in 2021 and 2022 at Ohio State, and both were All-Americans.

"I think the team as a whole it's a great situation for me," Harrison said of the Texans. "Being with a quarterback that you have rapport with and had success with in the past is always great too."

The No. 4 pick in the 2024 NFL draft joins Houston with an underwhelming career stat line of 1,578 yards, 13 touchdowns and 108 receptions in 33 games. When asked why he didn't produce in Arizona, he said he is "going to take accountability" but that he wants to keep specific information confidential.

"I think it's just a combination of everything," Harrison said. "I don't think I can pinpoint one thing. There's a lot of factors, and I think with any situation, you always want to take accountability for yourself.

"I think those things I'll keep to myself, truthfully. What I learned in Arizona, I definitely learned a lot. But like I said, I'm really just looking forward."

Harrison passed the physical on Monday and practiced with Houston for the first time Wednesday. There will be an acclimation process for him where he'll learn the playbook, but Ryans said he isn't worried about the learning part, citing Harrison's work ethic.

"It isn't hard when the player is attentive and he's locked in on getting the details down," Ryans said. "Marvin's first night here, he was with our assistant wide receiver coach Tiquan [Underwood] and they were grinding. They were working late at night. They were in the playbook grinding, and that allowed him to get a day ahead. And now, he was able to go out there today and just fit right in seamlessly."

Stroud said he was happy Houston included him in the discussion regarding acquiring the wide receiver. But now that Harrison is a Texan, the team will have to fit him into the offense.

Harrison is joining a wideout room led by Nico Collins, Xavier Hutchinson and Jaylin Noel. Stroud is humming through five weeks, ranking fifth in passing yards with 1,402.

The former college duo will lean on old experiences to rekindle chemistry, Stroud said, which is why he doesn't think the adjustment will take long.

"He's a really smart kid. I'm not worried about it," Stroud said of Harrison. "At the end of day, it's football. You run some very similar routes, just different ways, and I'm very vocal on how

articles.headline: Lisandro Martínez: I believe in 'everyone working to help' Man United 'move forward'
articles.description: Lisandro Martínez has said he believes in "my teammates, our manager and everyone working to help this club move forward" after he criticised Manchester United's hierarchy, including director of football Jason Wilcox in an explosive interview on Tuesday.
articles.headlineJa: リサンドロ・マルティネス「マン・ユナイテッドが『前進』するために協力する全員を信じている」
articles.descriptionJa: 火曜日の衝撃的なインタビューでジェイソン・ウィルコックス・フットボールディレクターを含むマンチェスター・ユナイテッドの上層部を批判したリサンドロ・マルティネスだが、「チームメイト、監督、そしてこのクラブを前進させるために尽力しているすべての人を信じている」と語った。
articles.body:
Lisandro Martínez has said he believes in "my teammates, our manager and everyone working to help this club move forward" after he criticised Manchester United's hierarchy, including director of football Jason Wilcox, in an explosive interview on Tuesday.

Following United's 2-0 defeat to Atletico Madrid in the Champions League, Martínez told Amazon Prime that he felt the club had failed to adequately strengthen the squad during the summer transfer window.

Sources told ESPN that United bosses were assessing Martínez's comments before deciding whether to take disciplinary action against the Argentina defender.

articles.headline: Man City can't compete with PSG, the Champions League's gold standard
articles.description: In dismantling Man City at the Etihad, PSG strengthened their claim to be Europe's finest -- and perhaps the best UCL team of all time.
articles.headlineJa: マン・シティはPSGに太刀打ちできない、彼らこそがチャンピオンズリーグの黄金基準だ
articles.descriptionJa: エティハド・スタジアムでマン・シティを圧倒したPSGは、欧州最強であるという主張を強めた。そして、おそらくUCL史上最高のチームである可能性さえ示している。
articles.body:
MANCHESTER, England -- Paris Saint-Germain laid out their credentials to win a third straight UEFA Champions League title by dismantling Manchester City at the Etihad Stadium.

The back-to-back European champions won 4-2 thanks in part to a blistering first-half performance that saw Luis Enrique's team go in at the break 3-0 up.

Pep Guardiola was back at the Etihad Stadium for the first time, in a show of support for the club in their first home game since the publication of the damning guilty verdict in their case with the Premier League. But City's former boss was stunned along with the rest of the home crowd as goals from Désiré Doué, Ousmane Dembélé and Vitinha saw PSG race to a three-goal lead during a brutal 19-minute spell.

Enzo Maresca made three changes at halftime, and his team improved after the break. Erling Haaland scored twice to become City's leading Champions League goal scorer and the youngest player to reach 60 Champions League goals, breaking Lionel Messi's record by a day.

But another PSG goal from Maghnes Akliouche put the brakes on a comeback, and it would have been worse for City had Ferran Torres not seen a late penalty saved by Gianluigi Donnarumma. -- Rob Dawson

Guardiola vs. Luis Enrique -- who's the best?

Guardiola returned to the Etihad for the first time since ending his 10-year reign as City manager in May, and he returned to see a master class ... by Luis Enrique's PSG.

The back-to-back Champions League winners reminded the world that they are the cream of Europe by humiliating City on their own turf. But was Guardiola also watching the best coach of his generation prove his caliber? Guardiola is often held up as the gold standard of coaches over the past decade and beyond, but is he really better than Luis Enrique?

Both men produce teams that play stunning football, and they have both won three Champions League titles. Guardiola and Luis Enrique can also claim the distinction of leading Barcelona to a treble. But Guardiola never managed to win successive Champions Leagues, which Luis Enrique achieved by guiding PSG to a successful defense of their crown last season. And if Luis Enrique can take PSG to a third successive Champions League title this season -- who would bet against him? -- then he would move ahead of Guardiola with four Champions League and secure a three-peat, something else Guardiola hasn't achieved.

While there can be no doubting Guardiola's pedigree, maybe even he has to take second billing to Luis Enrique. -- Mark Ogden

Man City get chastening Champions League lesson

Maresca said at his pre-match news conference on Tuesday that he didn't know whether City were close to the level of the reigning European champions or not. He has his answer now.

Maresca's team have been perfect in the Premier League so far this season, winning at Old Trafford and Anfield in the process. But this was a Champions League wake-up call.

articles.headline: Warriors' Kristaps Porzingis remains out indefinitely but will be around team
articles.description: Warriors center Kristaps Porzingis will remain out indefinitely with a private health-related issue but will be around the team.
articles.headlineJa: ウォリアーズのクリスタプス・ポルジンギス、引き続き無期限欠場となるがチームには帯同
articles.descriptionJa: ウォリアーズのセンター、クリスタプス・ポルジンギスは、プライベートな健康上の問題により引き続き無期限で欠場するが、チームには帯同する予定だ。
articles.body:
Kristaps Porzingis will remain out indefinitely with a private health-related issue, the Golden State Warriors announced Wednesday, but the veteran center will remain around the team.

"I'm working with doctors and experts to figure out how to be fully back to good health (as soon as possible)," Porzingis said on social media. "Honestly, I'm getting better and better. I just have to stay patient, and I believe I'll be feeling great again soon."

Porzingis called general manager Mike Dunleavy on the eve of training camp and informed the organization that he wouldn't be reporting. He didn't attend the team's trip to Hawaii and missed the first five preseason games.

While his coaches and teammates were in Las Vegas for a preseason game against the Los Angeles Lakers on Tuesday night, Porzingis returned to the Warriors' downtown San Francisco facility and met with Dunleavy and lead medical decision-maker Rick Celebrini.

In a statement, the Warriors said they'd keep the details of that meeting private, but Porzingis is expected to be in the facility and around the team as they wrap up preseason and prepare for the regular season opener next Wednesday in Los Angeles against the Lakers.

"It has definitely been frustrating dealing with some health stuff that you can't exactly pinpoint, on top of injuries throughout my career," Porzingis wrote in an X post. "So it has added up for sure, but we will get through it."

Porzingis is not yet cleared to practice and the team said it would update his "potential resumption of practice, playing status and timeline" whenever available and appropriate.

Two seasons ago, Porzingis contracted an upper respiratory virus while playing for the Boston Celtics, and he has since vaguely revealed the lingering impact it has had on his health and ability to consistently play NBA basketball.

Porzingis was limited to 34 games last season, split between the Atlanta Hawks and Warriors, who traded Jonathan Kuminga for him in February. Golden State then re-signed Porzingis to a two-year, $40 million deal this summer.

The contract was structured strategically to allow the Warriors to trade Porzingis at any point and limit their long-term downside. Only $3 million of the $20 million next season is guaranteed.

In his absence, coach Steve Kerr said he is leaning toward starting a smaller lineup of Stephen Curry, Brandin Podziemski, Gui Santos, Yaxel Lendeborg and Draymond Green.

articles.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Liverpool eye move for Juventus' Kalulu
articles.description: Liverpool are reportedly linked with a move for Juventus defender Pierre Kalulu. Transfer Talk has the latest.
articles.headlineJa: 移籍の噂・ニュース：リヴァプールがユヴェントスのカルルを狙う
articles.descriptionJa: リヴァプールがユヴェントスのディフェンダー、ピエール・カルルへの獲得に動いていると報じられている。Transfer Talkが最新情報を伝える。
articles.body:
Liverpool have shortlisted Juventus defender Pierre Kalulu, while Tottenham Hotspur defender Pedro Porro is being tracked by Real Madrid and Barcelona. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Liverpool have shortlisted Juventus defender Pierre Kalulu as a right back target for next summer, according to Tuttomercatoweb. The Reds admire the France international's versatility alongside Roma's Wesley, though Juventus are actively working to get Kalulu to sign an improved long-term contract.

- Tottenham Hotspur right back Pedro Porro is considering leaving the Premier League for a return to Spain, with Barcelona and Real Madrid monitoring his situation. Cadena Ser claims Madrid are leading the race, having monitored him before moving for Denzel Dumfries. Meanwhile, Sport reports that the 27-year-old, who is under contract until 2031, is also of interest to Barca, but the move is dependent on the club freeing up funds, while cheaper alternatives like Iván Fresneda are also being assessed.

Arsenal and Aston Villa hold an advantage over Newcastle United in the pursuit of RB Leipzig winger Antonio Nusa due to offering Champions League football, according to Football Insider. All three clubs are tracking the 21-year-old Norway international after his impressive start to the season saw him bag seven goal contributions in seven appearances.

- Bournemouth have softened their stance and are willing to allow midfielder Alex Scott to leave in January, reports the Daily Mail. However, the Cherries will demand a fee of over £100 million for the 23-year-old's transfer and will only permit a mid-season departure if their Premier League survival remains secure.

- Manchester United, Tottenham Hotspur, and Everton are keeping tabs on Dinamo Zagreb striker Dion Beljo ahead of a potential January move, per TEAMtalk. The 24-year-old Croatia international has scored 12 goals in his last 14 games, drawing scouting interest from Brentford, Manchester City, and Chelsea as well.

Other rumors

- Chelsea, Bayern Munich, Barcelona and Real Madrid have all added Brighton central defender Luka Vušković to their transfer shortlists ahead of next summer. (Ekrem Konur)

- Viking Stavanger defender Henrik Falchener is attracting interest across Europe after Southampton had a €9.5 million bid to sign him turned down in the summer. (Sky Germany)

- Bayern Munich and Paris Saint-Germain are monitoring Manchester United defender Leny Yoro amidst ongoing uncertainty surrounding his long-term future at Old Trafford. (TEAMtalk)

- Chelsea have joined Borussia Dortmund in scouting Philadelphia Union teenager Malik Jakupović, with the MLS club demanding over $10 million as a transfer fee. (TEAMtalk)

- Tottenham Hotspur are considering an €80 million January bid to sign Atlético Madrid midfielder Álex Baena to reinforce their attack following Xavi Simons' injury. (La Razón)

articles.headline: Real Madrid's late rally stuns Roma in 7-goal thriller
articles.description: Real Madrid scored three goals in seven minutes, all from corner kicks, to mount a dramatic comeback and claim a 4-3 win at AS Roma in the Champions League on Wednesday.
articles.headlineJa: レアル・マドリードが終盤に猛追し、7得点の乱打戦でローマを撃破
articles.descriptionJa: 水曜日のチャンピオンズリーグで、レアル・マドリードはすべてコーナーキックからの得点により、わずか7分間で3ゴールを奪う劇的な逆転劇を演じ、ASローマに4-3で勝利した。
articles.body:
Antonio Rüdiger's stoppage-time winner helped Real Madrid fight back from a two-goal deficit to earn Jose Mourinho a dramatic 4-3 victory at old club AS Roma in the Champions League.

Mourinho was on course for a dispiriting return to the Italian capital as Marten De Roon's 20th-minute opener and, after Kylian Mbappé 's leveller, a brace by Donyell Malen put Gian Piero Gasperini's team in complete control.

However, three goals from corners during a remarkable finale flipped the fixture on its head with Carlos Espi's goal after 83 minutes followed by late efforts from Endrick and Rüdiger to earn Real a stunning win.

Madrid were rocked hours before kick-off when they discovered Vinícius Júnior had been hit with a four-match ban in LaLiga for his sending-off in a 1-0 win over Villarreal, but he was included in the line-up for Mourinho's return to Rome.

The most eye-catching action early on at Stadio Olimpico was an enormous banner unveiled in the home end which showed Mourinho with the Conference League trophy he won during a successful three-year spell at Roma.

After Yan Diomande squandered a decent opening for the visitors, Roma were forced into a change after 17 minutes when Manu Koné was injured.

It failed to disrupt Gasperini's side as three minutes later they led through De Roon's strike.

Roma attacked at pace after Real gave away possession carelessly and Matìas Soulè teed up De Roon, who fired in a powerful left-footed strike which wrong-footed Thibaut Courtois thanks to a deflection.

Malen missed a great opportunity to double Roma's lead soon after and it came back to haunt the hosts with 25 minutes on the clock.

After Diomande flicked on a header, Mbappe rolled Mario Hermoso with ease and then sent a long-range strike beyond Pierluigi Gollini to mark his 100th Champions League match with a goal.

At the age of 27, Mbappé became the youngest player in history to reach a century of appearances in Europe's top competition.

Lionel Messi had set the previous record at age 28 against Roma in September 2015.

Jude Bellingham sent an effort wide before halftime, but it remained 1-1 until two goals in a decisive seven-minute spell in the second period decided the league phase contest.

Vinícius was involved, albeit for the wrong reasons, after his flick was intercepted and within seconds Rodrigo Mora had played in Malen, who took a touch and finished past Courtois in the 51st minute.

A third for Roma followed with 57 minutes played when one simple pass by Soule split the Real defence and Malen produced an accomplished finish to make it 3-1.

It was initially ruled out for offside before VAR intervened to award the goal and Mourinho responded with Vinicius hooked immediately for Endrick.

Real pushed for a way back and Gollini denied Mbappe twice in quick succession before substitute Espi provided a lifeline with seven minutes left when he tapped in after Endrick's header had been saved.

Two minutes later and Stadio Olimpico was silenced

articles.headline: Champions League recap: PSG score four past Man City, Madrid with comeback vs. Roma
articles.description: Paris Saint-Germain struck four past Manchester City while Real Madrid got a huge comeback against AS Roma on a Wednesday full of UEFA Champions League action.
articles.headlineJa: チャンピオンズリーグまとめ：PSGがマンチェスター・シティに4ゴール、マドリードはローマ戦で逆転勝利
articles.descriptionJa: UEFAチャンピオンズリーグの試合が盛り上がりを見せた水曜日、パリ・サンジェルマンがマンチェスター・シティに4ゴールを浴びせ、レアル・マドリードはASローマ相手に大逆転を遂げた。
articles.body:
THE CHAMPIONS!

It's another day, which means we had another round of Europe's best teams ready to battle it out on the biggest stage.

Matchday 2 of the 2026-27 UEFA Champions League continued Wednesday, with nine more games across the continent and plenty of mouthwatering clashes on the schedule.

Among the standout fixtures, Manchester City welcomed defending champions Paris Saint-Germain in a heavyweight showdown but were brought back down to earth as they lost 4-2. 

Real Madrid traveled to the Italian capital to face AS Roma and in a thrilling encounter, went from 3-1 down to win 4-3. Liverpool went to Austria to take on LASK in one of our early matches, where the Reds won 6-3 with Bradley Barcola getting a hat trick. In our other early match, Feyenoord defeated Como 3-2 in Rotterdam.

Elsewhere, Aston Villa hosted Fenerbahçe and ended up with a 6-0 win, while Borussia Dortmund made the trip to Norway to face Bodø/Glimt, but it was the hosts that ended up as 1-0 winners.

Finally, Shakhtar Donetsk defeated AEK Athens 3-1, Real Betis defeated FC Porto 3-2 and Stuttgart defeated Slovan Bratislava 3-0.

Enjoy all that happened from Wednesday's matches across Europe!

articles.headline: PSG hold off Man City's Haaland-inspired fightback
articles.description: Pep Guardiola's return ended in defeat on Wednesday as Manchester City lost 4-2 to Paris Saint-Germain in their first home match since being found guilty of serious financial irregularities.
articles.headlineJa: PSG、ハーランドが牽引したマンチェスター・シティの反撃を退ける
articles.descriptionJa: 重大な財務不正で有罪判決を受けて以来のホーム戦となった水曜日、ペップ・グアルディオラの復帰戦は、マンチェスター・シティがパリ・サンジェルマンに2-4で敗れるという結果に終わった。
articles.body:
Pep Guardiola's return ended in defeat on Wednesday as Manchester City lost 4-2 to Paris Saint-Germain in their first home match since being found guilty of serious financial irregularities.

The former City manager made his first visit to the Etihad Stadium since standing down last summer in a strong show of support for the club in light of last month's verdict from an independent commission.

His presence roused the fans, who also continued to show their defiance, but his night looked like falling flat as holders PSG swept into a 3-0 lead with a ruthless first-half display in the Champions League encounter.

But fired by a double from Erling Haaland, which saw the Norwegian become City's record goalscorer in the competition with 38 from 41 appearances, the hosts produced a superb fightback.

City spurned numerous chances, including hitting the woodwork twice, in a frantic second period, but with Maghnes Akliouche adding to earlier strikes from Désiré Doué, Ousmane Dembélé and Vitinha, PSG, who also missed a late penalty, held on.

It was City's first defeat since the Community Shield, ending a run of eight successive victories under Guardiola's successor Enzo Maresca.

It had seemed business as usual for City on Sunday as they ran out 3-0 winners at Liverpool, with their supporters making a strong show of their loyalty to the club in the face of the financial scandal.

That feeling was brought back to the Etihad with a huge "City Til I Die" tifo unfurled before kickoff, but on the field PSG were in no mood to play second fiddle.

The visitors served early warning as Warren Zaïre-Emery forced a save from former PSG goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma.

City wanted a penalty when Rayan Cherki went down in a challenge from Marquinhos but nothing was given, although the hosts almost got lucky when Matvei Safonov punched a corner onto his own bar.

PSG got into their stride, City struggled to contain them.

A lightning quick break brought the opening goal after 13 minutes as Doué cut inside from the left and beat Donnarumma inside his near post.

The second came just two minutes later as Dembélé crossed the ball from the right and continued his run to head home Doué's return ball.

Achraf Hakimi then planted a header against the post before the third arrived after 32 minutes as Vitinha smashed in from a Zaire-Emery lay-off. Hakimi should have added another, but shot straight at Donnarumma.

Maresca made a triple change at the break and the impact was immediate with one his substitutes, Iliman Ndiaye, crossing for Haaland to head home.

Antoine Semenyo also tested Safonov, but PSG soon hit back.

Donnarumma looked like he had saved Akliouche's long-range effort, but the ball took an unlucky bounce and spun back into the goal.

City continued to press forward with Enzo Fernández and Haaland both hitting the woodwork in quick succession.

PSG were breached again after 75 minutes when Haaland turned in from a Ayyoub Bouaddi pass, but the striker was denied

articles.headlineJa: NFLサバイバー・パワーランキング：今週ラムズ、ペイトリオッツ、コルツを起用すべき理由
articles.descriptionJa: ESPNによるNFLサバイバー・プールの戦略、予想、および第6週の推奨オプション・トップ6のランキング。
articles.body:
Welcome to ESPN NFL Survivor! The rules are simple: Pick one NFL team each week to win its game. If that team wins (or ties), you advance to the next week. If that team loses, you are out. The catch is that each team can be chosen only once. ESPN's game requires just one team each week, so that will be the focus of this column, though I will touch on other major contests.

For the third time in five weeks, the top-picked team in ESPN Survivor fell. This time, it was the Dallas Cowboys, who were picked by 35% of entries against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Since the loss came on Thursday, the concentrated selection on the Houston Texans and Cincinnati Bengals opened up other potential leverage opportunities.

However, two of the top potential low-future value picks both tied or lost in the Washington Commanders and Atlanta Falcons. Luckily for those who play ESPN Survivor, Commanders backers advanced to Week 6, unlike in Circa Survivor or Splash Sports. Entering Week 6, only 9.7% of entries in ESPN Survivor remain.

The biggest favorites in Week 6 are the Los Angeles Rams. While favorites of at least eight points are a paltry 5-5 outright, the four double-digit favorites this season are 4-0 outright.

In contests that require one pick per week, the Rams are the optimal pick, especially in smaller groups that are unlikely to last all season. However, in large pools, and pools with multi-pick weeks, I prefer to  save the Rams for later.

The Rams make a ton of sense as the biggest favorites of the week in their largest projected favorite role all season. However, Los Angeles is also projected to be favored in all but one or two of their remaining games, and as we get deeper into the season, having teams like the Rams available is valuable. That's especially true in Circa and Splash, which require multi-pick weeks, especially with the Rams projecting to be the biggest favorites on Circa's Thanksgiving slate.

The San Francisco 49ers and Kansas City Chiefs are both laying over a touchdown, but they have the two lowest availabilities among all remaining teams (Chiefs 37%, 49ers 44%). Both are fine contrarian picks this week, though both have significant future value, especially the 49ers.

The New England Patriots and Indianapolis Colts are the other strong choices this week. While they arguably have less win equity in Week 6, both have significantly less future value than the Rams, Chiefs and 49ers. However, both teams face the Dolphins in the next few weeks, so they will have other opportunities.

The Rams are the biggest favorites in the betting market by far in Week 6, and it's projected to be their largest favorite role all season. articles.headline: Erling Haaland breaks Lionel Messi record with goal against Paris Saint-Germain
articles.description: Erling Haaland broke Lionel Messi's record to be the youngest player to score 60 Champions League goals in Manchester City's clash with Paris Saint-Germain.
articles.headlineJa: アーリング・ハーランド、パリ・サンジェルマン戦の得点でリオネル・メッシの記録を更新
articles.descriptionJa: マンチェスター・シティ対パリ・サンジェルマンの一戦で、アーリング・ハーランドがチャンピオンズリーグで60ゴールを挙げた最年少選手となり、リオネル・メッシの記録を塗り替えた。
articles.body:
Erling Haaland broke Lionel Messi's record to become the youngest player to score 60 Champions League goals, after scoring in Manchester City's clash with Paris Saint-Germain on Wednesday.

Trailing 3-0 against the reigning European champions after a blistering first half from Luis Enrique's men, Haaland headed in Iliman Ndiaye's cross eight minutes into the second half.

It was a goal that gave City hope but on an individual basis, it was one which showed just how prolific Haaland has been ever since he first played in the Champions League for RB Salzburg.

He became the youngest ever player to reach 60 Champions League goals at 26 years and 85 days, beating one of the greatest ever players to play in the competition, Messi, by just one day (26y, 86d).

That was not the only record that goal broke for the Norwegian though, whose record against PSG is now five goals in four games after he scored a second later in the second half.

Haaland's 60th Champions League goal, which came in his 60th match, was his 37th in 41 appearances for City.

- Andy Burnham: Man City owners didn't mention Premier League charges in meeting

- Pep Guardiola makes first Etihad return since Man City guilty verdict

- Sources: Man United assessing Lisandro Martínez comments

That saw him go ahead of legendary City forward Sergio Aguero, who had 36 goals in 64 appearances during his time at the Etihad Stadium.

For a true sense of Haaland's dominance in the Champions League for Salzburg, Borussia Dortmund and City, here is a list of his closest competitors for goals in their first 60 appearances.

Most Goals in first 60 UCL appearances

- Erling Haaland 60

- Ruud van Nistelrooy 48

- Harry Kane 45

- Kylian Mbappé 40

- Lionel Messi 39

- Robert Lewandowski 39

articles.body:
With the preseason games coming to a close soon, the 2026-27 NBA season is less than a week away from tipping off.

How will LeBron James and Jaylen Brown look on the court in their new Philadelphia 76ers uniforms? What will Giannis Antetokounmpo's first season away from Milwaukee look like? And how will the other new faces in new places make their impact this season?

Check back here for all the latest buzz, news and reactions from our ESPN NBA insiders, with the latest info at the top:

Trade tracker | Transactions | Offseason buzz

Depth charts | Trade machine | More

Oct. 14

Hoop Collective: The biggest questions in the NBA's Central Division

Brian is joined by ESPN's Vincent Goodwill and Tim MacMahon to preview the NBA's Central Division, including the biggest questions facing the five teams. Is this another make-or-break season for the Cleveland Cavaliers? Will the Detroit Pistons repeat their 2025-26 success? And, can Tyrese Haliburton's return vault the Indiana Pacers back up the Eastern Conference standings? They tackle all this and more in the latest episode of the Hoop Collective podcast.

Topics:

0:15: Our 2026-27 Central Division preview

4:25: Lots of big questions for the Pistons

11:43: Make or break season for the Cavaliers

27:50: Can Haliburton bring back the Pacers?

35:30: Bucks post-Giannis future looks murky

42:05: Young talent is intriguing with the Bulls

Windhorst on if the Cavaliers can improve their roster: "Jarrett Allen is the guy that they would have to do something with. And the thing about it is that they can't trade Jarrett Allen because you'd need a franchise center. And that means Evan Mobley would probably have to be your franchise center.

"First off, if you're trading Jarrett Allen, are you upgrading at center for trading Jarrett Allen? No, you're probably upgrading somewhere else and you're asking Evan Mobley to play center. And Evan Mobley has not proven, even though a lot of people believe that he would be at his best playing full-time stretch center, [he can do that]. That's not something they've been able to get Evan to do consistently well. But that's the move that they have. The move that they have if they have to do something is to look at Jarrett Allen.

"But we'll see how that plays out. The Cavs are in a tough spot in that they are going to be expected to improve on last season, which the pathway to improve on a conference final season, it's a narrow path. And they're doing it in a much more competitive Eastern Conference landscape."

Latest episodes of the 'Hoop Collective' podcast

Oct. 13

Pritchard agrees to two-year extension in Boston

Boston Celtics' guard Payton Pritchard has agreed a to a two-year, $44.2 million extension with the franchise, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. Pritchard averaged career highs in points (17), assists (5.2) and rebounds (3.9) last season.

articles.headline: New era begins as Jayson Tatum and the Celtics embark on 1st season without Jaylen Brown
articles.description:
Boston Celtics 
              Last season: 58-26, lost to Philadelphia in first round of playoffs.
articles.body:
Boston Celtics 
              Last season: 58-26, lost to Philadelphia in first round of playoffs.


              COACH: Joe Mazzulla (5th season, 238-90).


              SEASON OPENER: Oct. 20 at Detroit.


              DEPARTURES: F Jaylen Brown, C Nikola Vucevic, F Anfernee Simons.


              ADDITIONS: F Paul George, C Mitchell Robinson, G Mike Conley Jr. 


              What to expect 
              It's a new era in Boston following the offseason trade of Brown to the Philadelphia 76ers. Only a few pieces remain from the core of the Celtics 2023-24 championship team. And there are lots of questions surrounding how this new version of the team will look without the homegrown tandem of Brown and Tatum that literally grew into the pillars of the franchise. Mazzulla has proven an ability to get the best out of what he has to work with, as evidenced in how the team played without Tatum last season as he recovered from rupturing his right Achilles tendon 17 months ago. But this may be the biggest test of Mazzulla's tenure as he looks to not only integrate new pieces, but make adjustments to an offense that has previously relied so heavily on 3-point shooting.


              Strengths and weaknesses


              The good: It starts with Tatum, who looks to be fully back to himself physically after rehabiliation from his surgery caused him to miss all but 16 regular season games and then Game 7 of their playoff loss to the 76ers because of a knee stiffness. George also enters the season healthy and at age 36 is poised to build off his strong playoff performance with the 76ers last season. Robinson’s presence brings an instant upgrade in rim protection, while also giving this group some great depth and options at center. Neemias Queta will likely remain the starter, but with plenty of support from both Robinson and Luka Garza. 


              The not-so-good: Brown’s departure breaks up the dynamic between he and Tatum that worked so well for nine seasons and eventually netted Boston its 18th NBA title. George says he’s more than willing to yield to Tatum, but that will put the weight on Tatum’s shoulders to carry the team, a burden he hasn’t had to bear alone yet during his career. 


              Players to watch
              Derrick White has tweaked the mechanics of his shot after a rough shooting year and will get more opportunities with Brown gone. Payton Pritchard started a career-high 50 games and average career bests in points (17.0), assists (5.2) and rebounds (3.9) last season coming off winning NBA Sixth Man of the Year honors in 2024-25. Last season also showed that he plays better coming off the bench, a role he’s expected to remain in barring injuries. Hugo Gonzalez also looks more skilled and comfortable at the NBA level as he prepares for Year 2.
